answer.label: In short
answer.lead: Study abroad marketing is the work of reaching students and parents who are comparing countries, courses and intakes, and getting them to a counselling session. It combines search by country and course, webinars and fairs, a qualifying enquiry form, fast counsellor follow-up and honest claims about admissions and visas.
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) markets study abroad consultancies and education agents in India, connecting ads to a CRM so counsellors can follow every lead.

blocks.h: How study abroad decisions are made
paras: A student and parents compare countries, universities, costs, scholarships and visa routes over months. They search on phones, join webinars and ask agents, alumni and friends.
Timing follows application intakes and test dates, and trust matters because the decision is large.
blocks.cap: A nurture series for an applicant.

blocks.h: The problem that keeps coming back
paras: Consultancies often receive many unqualified enquiries, spread counsellor time thin, and lose students who need months of nurture. Some also face complaints about over-promising.

The fix is to qualify by country, course, budget and timeline, route to the right counsellor, nurture until the intake, and avoid promising admissions or visas. See the education marketing overview and the guides.

callout.title: Never promise an outcome.
callout.text: We do not promise admissions, scholarships or visas. Ads must not either.
